entries.title: Acceptable Documents for Legal Presence
entries.summary: Lists acceptable documents to prove legal presence in the US for driver license and ID card issuance, including requirements for immigrants, non-immigrants, and various visa categories with specific document combinations and issuance term limits.

keyFacts.claim: All U.S. citizens, immigrants, and work-authorized non-immigrants must show proof of a social security number for Florida credentials.
U.S. citizens and immigrants age 79 and under receive eight-year licenses, while those 80 and older receive six-year licenses.
Non-immigrants receive licenses valid only through their authorized stay date, not exceeding one year from issuance.
Canadian citizens with valid passports receive six-month driver licenses or ID cards.
Expired I-551 Permanent Resident Cards may be used if the customer's immigrant status verifies through the VLS system.
Border Crossing Cards must be accompanied by an I-94 and cannot be accepted alone for legal presence.

entries.title: Cashiering Procedures (CA01)
entries.summary: Procedures for payment processing at driver license service centers, including accepted payment methods (cash, check, credit cards, Apple/Google Pay), transaction review requirements, and cashiering workflows for completing transactions.

keyFacts.claim: All customers are required to review and accept their transaction before beginning the cashiering procedure.
Driver license service centers accept American Express, Discover, MasterCard, Visa, and Apple/Google Pay for payment of services.
Credit cards can only be accepted if the card holder is present and the name, signature, and expiration must be verified.
Personal checks must be imprinted with check writer's name, no more than the amount of the transaction, and signed by the person whose name is imprinted on the check.
Bills $50 or higher in denomination must be verified using a counterfeit detection pen and black light before acceptance.

entries.title: Revenue Management (CA02)
entries.summary: Internal procedures for cash handling, payment methods, and revenue reporting at driver license service centers. Covers accepted payment types including cash, checks, money orders, and credit cards, plus counterfeit detection requirements.

keyFacts.claim: All accepted forms of payment must be drawn on U.S. banks only.
Bills $50 or higher in denomination must be verified using a counterfeit detection pen or light.
Personal checks must be imprinted with the check writer's name and may not exceed the transaction amount.
Money orders and traveler's checks may not exceed $100 over the amount of the total transaction.
Foreign currency, foreign checks, and foreign traveler's checks including Canadian are not acceptable.

entries.title: Refund Requests (CA03)
entries.summary: Process for requesting refunds when customers were incorrectly charged fees for driver license services. Covers common refund scenarios, required documentation, submission process, and 4-8 week processing timeframes.

keyFacts.claim: Customers can request refunds for overpayments, payments where none was due, and payments made in error by completing Form HSMV 73644.
100% disabled veterans should not be charged fees for driver license services when proper documentation is provided.
Veterans with proper designation documentation should not be charged fees for driver license services.
CDL holders downgrading to Class E licenses should not be charged a fee when no other changes are made.
Refund requests should be mailed to Division of Motorist Services, P.O. Box 5775, Tallahassee, Florida 32314.
Customers should expect 4-8 weeks processing time before receiving a refund check or denial notice.

entries.title: Customer Search (CI01)
entries.summary: Explains how staff search for existing customer records using driver license number, Social Security number, or name and date of birth. Covers requirements for out-of-state customers and document scanning procedures.

keyFacts.claim: Customers can be searched using their Florida driver license or ID card number, Social Security number, or name and date of birth.
A 'No SSN' checkbox is available for customers who are not eligible for a Social Security number.
Out-of-state customers must have their credential information entered in designated out-of-state fields during the search process.
All documents required as part of a transaction must be scanned, except for any documents indicating medical information.
The system searches multiple databases including ORION, PDPS, SPEXS, and SSA to verify customer information and check for sanctions.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Creating a Customer (CI02)
entries.summary: Requirements for creating new driver license or ID card records, including required personal information, documentation for REAL ID compliance, social security number requirements, name change procedures, and out-of-state license handling.

keyFacts.claim: Customers must present all REAL ID requirements including documents to establish legal presence, name, date of birth, proof of social security number, and residential address.
Non-immigrants without social security numbers must obtain a letter from SSA indicating they are not eligible to obtain an SSN.
Non-immigrants applying for a commercial learner's permit or commercial driver license must present a social security number prior to issuance.
Customers who want to use a name different from their primary identification document must provide an approved name change document.
All required documents must be scanned except for documents containing medical information.

entries.title: Customer Eligibility (CI03)
entries.summary: Eligibility requirements for ID cards, Class E licenses, learner permits, motorcycle licenses, and CDLs including age, identity documents, Social Security, address proof, education courses, parental consent, and exam requirements.

keyFacts.claim: ID cards require customers to be at least 5 years old, except those eligible for disabled parking permits may get an ID card regardless of age.
Class E learner's license minimum age is 15 years, and Class E license minimum age is 16 years.
Persons under 18 must hold a learner's license for at least 12 months with no moving violations before getting a Class E license.
CDL applicants must be at least 18 years old and customers aged 18-20 are restricted to intrastate only and cannot get hazmat endorsements.
Traffic Law Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE) is required for persons 18+ who have never held a driver license, while Driver Education Traffic Safety (DETS) is required for persons under 18.
CDL applicants must demonstrate ability to understand and respond to verbal commands in English during skills testing.

entries.title: License Details and Messages (CI04)
entries.summary: Explains system messages customers may encounter during driver license transactions, including immediate action required, action required, and informational messages. Covers vision/medical indicators, license details display, and scanning requirements.

keyFacts.claim: Customers with fraud investigation pending messages will be denied issuance of any credential.
Customers with possible imposter messages must provide a primary identification document before any credential can be issued.
CDL holders with expired medical certificates must provide valid medical certification or downgrade their license class.
Customers who exceed convenience renewal limits must visit a driver license field office or tax collector office for service.
Customers with residential address changes must provide proof of address documents during their transaction.
All required transaction documents must be scanned except those containing medical information.

entries.title: Personal Information (CI05)
entries.summary: Rules for updating personal information on driver licenses and ID cards, including name changes, address changes, requirements for homeless customers, and procedures for correcting deceased status errors.

keyFacts.claim: Two proof of residential address documents are required to change a customer's address.
A customer's full legal name must be taken from primary identification documents and additional name change documents may be required.
If a customer's name exceeds character limits on the card, the system will automatically truncate the middle name to its first initial, then the first name if needed.
Customers incorrectly marked as deceased who reside in Florida can visit a service center or tax collector office with photo ID to have the error corrected.
The transient field is used for persons that are homeless.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Sanctions (CI06)
entries.summary: Administrative sanctions against drivers who fail to operate safely or follow motor vehicle laws, including suspensions, revocations, cancellations, and disqualifications. Covers reinstatement requirements, hardship hearings, ignition interlock devices, and driving school completion.

keyFacts.claim: Customers with open Florida sanctions from 15 years or less must pay applicable fees regardless of being licensed by another state.

Customers with open Florida sanctions from more than 15 years ago can have reinstatement fees and compliance requirements waived if they were licensed in another state after the sanction expiration date.
All sanctions are effective at 12:00 am on the sanction effective date.
Florida law requires customers to surrender all driver licenses to FLHSMV whenever their driving privilege is cancelled, revoked, or suspended.
Drivers aged 15-17 who accumulate six or more points in a 12-month period must appear within 10 days to receive a Business Purposes Only restriction for at least one year.

Ignition interlock devices are required for certain DUI convictions with specific compliance periods: first conviction with .15 BAC or minor in vehicle requires at least 6 months, second conviction requires at least 1 year.

entries.title: Driver License Cancellations (CI06A)
entries.summary: Comprehensive guide to driver license cancellation codes, reasons for cancellation (fraud, missing documents, unpaid fees, failed exams, etc.), and reinstatement requirements including fees and documentation needed to restore driving privileges.

keyFacts.claim: FLHSMV may cancel driver licenses if the licensee was not entitled to issuance, provided false information, committed fraud, or failed to pay correct fees.
Customers with altered birth dates on license applications must provide original or certified primary identification documents to reinstate their license.
Bounced check payments result in license cancellation and require payment to the Cashier Refund Section via cashier's check, money order, or credit card.
Court-ordered ignition interlock device violations require proof of IID installation and restart the IID time period for DUI offenses after October 1, 2008.
Customers who voluntarily surrender their license can be re-issued without examinations, but the license holder must personally surrender it.
Standard reinstatement fees include $48 original license fee, $25 replacement fee, and $6.25 tax collector service fee with no cancellation removal fee.

entries.title: CDL Disqualifications (CI06B)
entries.summary: Details CDL disqualification periods, reinstatement requirements, and fees for various violations including DUI, railroad crossing violations, medical certification failures, and other commercial driving offenses. Covers downgrade options to Class E license during disqualification.

keyFacts.claim: CDL holders can downgrade to a Class E driver license during disqualification to operate non-commercial vehicles.
Most CDL disqualifications require a $75.00 reinstatement fee and are not eligible for early reinstatement.
Failure to maintain current medical certification results in indefinite CDL disqualification until requirements are met.
Railroad crossing violations result in escalating disqualification periods: 60 days for first offense, 120 days for second, one year for third within 3 years.
Certain felony convictions involving controlled substances or human trafficking result in permanent CDL disqualification with no reinstatement options.

entries.title: Driver License Suspensions (CI06C)
entries.summary: Comprehensive guide to driver license suspension types, reasons, periods, reinstatement requirements, and fees. Covers point suspensions, DUI-related suspensions, court-directed suspensions, fraud suspensions, and various violation-based suspensions with specific reinstatement procedures.

keyFacts.claim: Point suspensions occur when accumulating 12 points in 12 months (30-day suspension), 18 points in 18 months (3-month suspension), or 24 points in 36 months (1-year suspension).
DUI administrative suspensions are 6 months for first offense and 1 year for subsequent offenses, with a required DUI course for reinstatement.
Driver license fraud suspensions last one year and require retaking all knowledge and skills exams for reinstatement.
Most suspensions allow hardship hearings through Bureau of Administrative Review (B.A.R.) for early reinstatement consideration.
Standard suspension reinstatement fee is $45.00 plus $25.00 replacement fee and $6.25 tax collector service fee.

entries.title: Driver License Revocations (CI06D)
entries.summary: Details various driver license revocation types, their periods, reinstatement requirements, and fees. Covers DUI, felony, court-directed, and other serious violations that result in license revocation and the process to restore driving privileges.

keyFacts.claim: A fourth DUI conviction results in permanent revocation, but customers can apply for early reinstatement after 5 years through a Bureau of Administrative Review hearing.
DUI revocations require completion of a DUI course and payment of a $75 revocation reinstatement fee plus $130 administrative fee.
Habitual Traffic Offender revocation occurs after 15 moving violations or 3 major violations within 5 years and requires ADI course completion.
Court-directed revocations may extend beyond statutory minimums and require separate reinstatement fees for each revocation type.
Customers with medical or vision-related revocations must submit required reports to the appropriate FLHSMV section for reinstatement authorization.

entries.title: Financial Responsibility (CI06E)
entries.summary: Financial responsibility requirements for Florida drivers, including insurance coverage minimums, sanctions for uninsured driving, SR22/FR44 certificates, and clearance procedures for various violation types.

keyFacts.claim: Florida requires minimum insurance coverage of $10,000 bodily injury liability per person, $20,000 per occurrence, and $10,000 property damage liability.
Financial responsibility suspensions remain in effect for two to three years unless compliance requirements are satisfied.
SR22 certificates must be maintained for three years from the original suspension date and are required for uninsured violations.
Electronic proof of insurance is acceptable for clearing FR sanctions if it contains the same information as a paper insurance card.
Tag surrender can prevent PIP cancellation sanctions when voluntarily canceling mandatory insurance coverage.

entries.title: Correspondence Codes (CI07)
entries.summary: Reference guide for correspondence codes that appear on driving records to document actions, events, and decisions affecting driver license transactions. Includes codes for hearings, medical reviews, sanctions, and administrative actions.

keyFacts.claim: Correspondence entries are placed on driving records to record actions or events that may affect future transactions.
A tax collector service fee of $6.25 applies if applicable to correspondence-related transactions.
All documents required as part of a transaction must be scanned unless they contain medical information.
Customers may be required to complete various courses like ADI, BDI, or DUI school based on their driving record.
Administrative suspensions and disqualifications can be invalidated or sustained through formal or informal review processes.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Medical Requirements & Re-Exams (CI08)
entries.summary: Medical screening requirements, five-day letters for re-testing, medical review processes, voluntary license surrender, and fees for customers with physical or mental conditions that may affect driving ability.

keyFacts.claim: Customers with static medical conditions like paralysis, amputation, or severe arthritis may receive a five-day letter requiring re-examination within five working days.
Customers who admit to epilepsy, fainting, dizzy spells, progressive neurological diseases, or severe psychiatric disorders within the last two years must undergo medical review.
Customers may voluntarily surrender their driver license if they feel unable to operate a motor vehicle safely, but only the license holder themselves can make this surrender.
If a customer fails required medical re-examinations, their driving privilege will be suspended and their Florida license will be retained by the office.
No fees are charged for examinations required due to five-day letters or medical re-exams, but replacement license fees and tax collector service fees still apply.

entries.title: Short History (CI09)
entries.summary: Describes the Short History record that contains a customer's name cross-reference, current address, and current/previous driver license and ID card issuances. Includes a $6.25 Tax Collector service fee if applicable.

keyFacts.claim: The Short History record shows names previously used by the customer on their Florida driver license or ID card.
The Short History displays the customer's current mailing and residential address.
Information about current and previous driver license and ID card issuances is included in the Short History.
All documents required as part of a transaction must be scanned, except for documents indicating medical information.
A Tax Collector service fee of $6.25 may apply if applicable.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Exams (CI10)
entries.summary: Covers exam requirements, scoring, and procedures for driver license testing including vision screening, knowledge exams, skills tests, interpreters, parent proctoring, exam reciprocation from other states/countries, and associated fees.

keyFacts.claim: All examinations must be administered in English, with interpreters only allowed to translate to American Sign Language for Class E exams.
Class E knowledge and skills exams do not expire and can be applied to transactions as long as evidence exists in the system.
Commercial driver license knowledge and skills exams must be applied to issuance within one year of the pass date.
Customers under 18 taking online tests must have a parent, guardian, or responsible adult proctor the exam.
Knowledge and skills exams are reciprocated from valid driver licenses issued by US states, territories, Canada, Germany, France, Taiwan, and South Korea.
Customers selected for random retesting are not charged retest fees for their first retest attempt but pay fees for subsequent exams.

entries.title: Vision Screening (CI10A)
entries.summary: Vision requirements and screening procedures for driver licenses, including minimum standards (20/70 both eyes together), restrictions for corrective lenses, and requirements for customers 80+ years old to have vision exams by licensed professionals.

keyFacts.claim: Vision is approved if both eyes together are 20/70 or better, regardless of individual eye acuity, except if one eye is blind or 20/200 or worse, then the other eye must be 20/40 or better.
Customers 80 years or older must have vision exams conducted by credentialing personnel, licensed physicians, optometrists, or licensed physicians at federally established veterans' hospitals.
CDL applicants must meet federal vision standard of 20/40 in each eye with best correction, and school bus drivers cannot receive waivers for vision requirements.
Customers wearing contact lenses will be restricted to corrective lenses while driving, including those wearing lenses for cosmetic purposes only.
Customers who do not meet minimum vision standards must be issued a field revocation order for inadequate vision and surrender all licenses and temporary permits.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Knowledge Exams (CI10B)
entries.summary: Requirements for driver license knowledge exams including age limits, testing procedures, retesting rules, fees, and exam content for Class E and CDL licenses. Covers oral exams, interpreter services, and cheating policies.

keyFacts.claim: Class E knowledge exams can be taken starting at age 14 years, 6 months or older.
CDL knowledge exams can be taken starting at age 17 years, 6 months or older.
Knowledge exams have a 60-minute time limit, with failure to complete resulting in automatic exam failure.
Customers are limited to two attempts per day on each type of knowledge exam at driver license or tax collector offices.
Class E knowledge exams do not expire, but CDL exams cannot be over one year old.
Knowledge exams require a passing score of 80% for both Class E and CDL exams.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Skills Exam (CI10C)
entries.summary: Requirements and procedures for Class E driving skills exams, including vehicle inspection, course requirements, safety protocols, and scoring criteria. Covers who can administer exams, required maneuvers, and disqualification conditions.

keyFacts.claim: Customers must successfully complete knowledge and vision exams before taking a skills exam, or present a valid Florida or out-of-state Class E Learner's License.
Vehicles used for skills exams must have valid Florida license plates and proof of Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and Property Damage Liability (PDL) insurance.
Skills exams will not be given if the vehicle fails inspection for defective horn, mirrors, directional signals, steering, brakes, tires, brake lights, or expired license plates.
Customers under 18 must hold a Learner's license for at least 12 months with no moving violations and complete 50 hours of supervised driving (10 hours at night) before getting a full license.
Skills exams include specific maneuvers: straight-in parking, turnabout, quick stop, backing, and stop/start on grade, plus evaluation of turns, stop signs, and traffic lights.

entries.title: MV Ownership (CI11)
entries.summary: Describes how motor vehicle ownership information is displayed and used during driver license transactions, including vehicle registration details, title information, and owner data that may be referenced for financial responsibility suspensions.

keyFacts.claim: Motor vehicle information may be used by staff processing driver license transactions to provide information about vehicle registration.
Vehicle ownership information can be used to establish ownership dates for financial responsibility suspensions.
The Motor Vehicle Ownership Tab displays all vehicles registered or titled to the customer.
Vehicle information includes VIN/HIN number, year, make, license plate, body type, decal information, and color.
Title information includes title status, use designation, odometer date and mileage, title issue date, and previous state information.

entries.title: National Law Enforcement Telecommunication System - NLETS (CI12)
entries.summary: Describes NLETS system used to check driving records from other states during Florida license applications. Includes automatic NDR/PDPS searches for original and renewal applications, with $6.25 Tax Collector service fee if applicable.

keyFacts.claim: A NDR/PDPS search is automatically run when a customer applies for an original or renewal of a Florida driver license.
NLETS can be used to retrieve customer's driver license information from other states to potentially waive Traffic Law Substance Abuse and Education (TLSAE) licensing requirements.
NLETS provides additional information when another state shows the customer's driving privilege is revoked, canceled, or denied.
NLETS is only used for verification of previous license issuance and does not regulate a customer's eligibility status.
Eligibility status is determined by the NDR/PDPS response, not NLETS verification.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: AAMVA Results (CI13)
entries.summary: Explains how out-of-state driving records are checked through AAMVA systems when applying for Florida licenses. Covers eligibility requirements, status codes, and what happens if you have suspensions or violations in other states.

keyFacts.claim: When applying for any Florida driver license, your record is automatically checked against national databases to see if you have licenses or violations in other states.
If your out-of-state status shows as suspended, revoked, cancelled, disqualified, or not eligible, a Florida driver license may not be issued.
For CDL applications, your status must be completely clear in both national systems - letters of clearance are not acceptable unless authorized by headquarters.
If you're ineligible due to out-of-state issues, you must present a clearance letter from the problem state dated within the last 30 days.
A disqualification in another state prevents CDL issuance but may still allow a regular Class E license to be issued.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Photo and Signature Requirements (CI14)
entries.summary: Requirements for photos and signatures on Florida driver licenses and ID cards, including acceptable appearance standards, religious/medical exceptions, oath administration, and parental consent procedures for minors.

keyFacts.claim: All Florida driver licenses and ID cards require a full facial photograph with the customer looking directly at the camera.
Face coverings, veils, and hats must be removed for photos, though religious head coverings that don't obscure facial features are permitted.
Sunglasses may only be worn in photos if the customer is legally blind, and eye patches are allowed for medical conditions.
All customers must take an oath swearing the truth of their application information before credential issuance.
Parents or guardians may sign ID card applications for children who cannot sign or make a mark themselves.

entries.title: Automated Driver License Testing System - ITI (CR01A)
entries.summary: Rules for knowledge exams including 60-minute time limits, available languages (Arabic, Chinese, English, Haitian Creole, Spanish, Russian for Class E; English/Spanish for CDL), printed exam options for customers with learning disabilities or needing translators, and exam fees.

keyFacts.claim: All knowledge exams have a 60-minute time limit that starts when exam instructions are displayed.
Customers with learning disabilities or using translators qualify for printed tests with extended time.
Class E knowledge exams are available in Arabic, Chinese, English, Haitian Creole, Spanish, and Russian.
CDL knowledge exams are available in English and Spanish, but original Hazardous Material exams must be taken in English.
If an exam is not completed within 60 minutes, it automatically results in a failure and counts toward exam attempts.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Automated Driver License Testing System - IDEMIA (CR01B)
entries.summary: Rules for knowledge exams including time limits, available languages, fees, and requirements for customers with learning disabilities or needing translators. Covers Class E and CDL knowledge testing procedures and language options.

keyFacts.claim: All knowledge exams have a 60-minute time limit that starts when exam instructions are displayed.
Customers with learning disabilities or using translators qualify for exceptions to the 60-minute time limit and must be given a printed test.
Class E knowledge exams are available in Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, Spanish, Russian, and Vietnamese.
CDL knowledge exams are available in English and Spanish, but original Hazardous Material exams must be taken in English.
If a customer does not complete the exam within 60 minutes, it automatically records as a failure and counts toward exam attempts with re-exam fees applying.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Be on The Look Out (BOLO) (CR02)
entries.summary: Explains the BOLO system used to flag customer records for special attention. Covers when BOLOs are placed, how they appear to customers during transactions, associated fees, and requirements for resolution before services can be completed.

keyFacts.claim: A BOLO (Be On the Look Out) flag can be placed on a customer's driver license record to alert staff of special circumstances or requirements.
When a BOLO is active on a customer's record, staff will see a 'Check Correspondence' message directing them to review the correspondence details.
BOLO correspondence must be removed once the customer has complied with the requirements detailed in the BOLO.
All documents required as part of a transaction must be scanned, except those containing medical or vision information.
A Tax Collector Service Fee of $6.25 may apply to BOLO-related transactions if applicable.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Emergency Contact Information (CR03)
entries.summary: Rules for adding emergency contact information to Florida credentials. Customers can provide up to two emergency contacts online or during credential issuance. Information is confidential and only available to law enforcement in emergencies. $6.25 tax collector fee applies.

keyFacts.claim: Customers holding a Florida credential can add or update emergency contact information online or during credential issuance at a service center or tax collector office.
Customers may provide up to two emergency contacts, each requiring name, relationship, address, city, state, zip and at least one telephone number.
Emergency contact information is limited to US addresses and telephone numbers only.
Emergency contact information is confidential and only available to law enforcement officers in cases of emergency.
During credential issuance, staff are required to ask customers if they would like to add or change emergency contact information.

feeAmounts.label: Tax collector service fee if applicable

entries.title: Exceptions (CR04)
entries.summary: Explains when customers can use alternative documents when required ID documents aren't available due to circumstances beyond their control. Covers three exception levels, special cases for older customers, expired passports, name changes, and homeless situations.

keyFacts.claim: Customers born on or before 1935 can use secondary identification with their date of birth if they cannot obtain a birth certificate.
Expired U.S. passports may be accepted as primary identification with a Level I exception.
Customers born on or before 1945 can use secondary identification if they cannot obtain a birth certificate, requiring manager approval.
Hospital birth certificates may be accepted with a Level II manager exception.
Church marriage certificates may be accepted as name change documents for U.S. citizens with manager approval.
Homeless customers unable to obtain homeless certification may self-certify on a Certification of Address form with manager approval.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Inventory Management System (CR05)
entries.summary: Internal procedures for managing driver license and ID card inventory, including card printing supplies, defective card handling, and destruction processes. Not directly customer-facing but affects service availability.

keyFacts.claim: The card print vendor ensures each field office maintains a 30-day supply of driver license and ID card inventory.
Cards that get damaged during processing or printed incorrectly are marked for destruction and stored securely.
If the office scanner is not working, most inventory functions can be completed by typing embedded inventory numbers instead of scanning barcodes.
Card packs must contain exactly 50 cards and be visually inspected for damage before being placed into use.
If the office cannot complete beginning of day inventory procedures, cards can still be issued from an inventory state to serve customers.

entries.title: Online Appointment Services (CR06)
entries.summary: Describes online appointment systems available for scheduling visits to driver license service centers, including Ventus for Broward, Miami-Dade, and Volusia counties, and the discontinued OASIS system.

keyFacts.claim: Ventus is an Internet application that allows the public to schedule appointments at service centers in Broward, Miami-Dade, or Volusia County.
Online Appointment Service and Information System (OASIS) was decommissioned in December 2020.
Some Tax Collectors use their own appointment systems instead of state-provided systems.
The appointment systems are used by service centers to manage customer visits.

entries.title: Paperless Waiver System (CR07)
entries.summary: Explains how third-party test results are accessed and applied to driver license transactions, including exam retention periods, retest requirements, and fees for failed exams taken through third-party testers.

keyFacts.claim: Class E knowledge and skills exams do not have an expiration and can be applied as long as there is evidence in the system.
Commercial driver license knowledge and skills exams must be applied to an issuance within one year of the pass date.
The third-party testing system randomly selects every 40th Class E exam for retesting, which requires passing an additional test at a service center or tax collector office.
Customers do not pay a retest fee for the first required retest for quality control, but must pay the retest fee for subsequent exams if they fail the first retest.
A receipt from a third-party tester is for information purposes only and is not accepted as evidence of a test having been passed.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Verification of Lawful Status (CR08)
entries.summary: Requirements for verifying U.S. citizenship, immigrant, and non-immigrant status for driver license and ID card issuance, including required documents, verification processes, and exceptions for different legal presence categories.

keyFacts.claim: All U.S. citizens must show proof of social security number for driver license or ID card issuance.
All immigrants must show proof of social security number for credential issuance.
All non-immigrants with work-authorized immigration status must show proof of social security number.
Non-immigrant customers must have 61 days or more authorized in the U.S. to be issued a credential.
Canadian citizens providing a valid Canadian passport are eligible for credential issuance with a 6-month expiration date.
If lawful status cannot be verified through VLS, a 60-day temporary permit is issued while additional verification is processed.

entries.title: ID Cards (EO01)
entries.summary: Requirements, eligibility, and fees for Florida ID cards including age requirements, document needs, no-fee options for homeless/poverty/veterans, renewal procedures, and issuance periods. Cannot hold both driver license and ID card.

keyFacts.claim: Florida law prohibits holding both a Florida ID card and a driver license from Florida or any other state - the existing credential must be surrendered.
ID cards require minimum age of 5 years, except those eligible for disabled parking permits can get ID cards at any age.
ID cards are valid for 8 years if age 15 or older, 4 years if age 5-14, and up to 1 year for non-immigrants based on immigration document expiration.
Homeless individuals can get no-fee ID cards with certification from homeless shelter, school district liaison, or DCF within 90 days of issuance.
Customers at or below 100% federal poverty level qualify for no-fee ID cards with tax return or Access Florida Benefits documentation.
Florida voters experiencing financial hardship can get no-fee ID cards by presenting valid voter registration card and self-attesting to hardship.

entries.title: Class E Driver License (EO02)
entries.summary: Requirements, procedures, and fees for Class E driver licenses including original issuance, renewals, replacements, temporary permits, learner's license upgrades, and delinquent renewal options. Covers age requirements, vision screening, and driving restrictions for minors.

keyFacts.claim: The minimum age to hold a Class E driver license is 16 years of age.
Customers who are 79 years of age and under will be issued a driver license valid for eight years, while customers 80 and older receive six-year licenses.
A temporary permit may be issued for up to 60 days to customers who cannot provide REAL ID compliant documents if their current license is valid or expired 60 days or less.
Delinquent renewals processed up to one year after expiration incur a $15.00 fee, which can be waived by taking the Class E knowledge exam.
Persons under 18 must hold a learner's license for at least 12 months with no moving violations before upgrading to Class E, unless they reach their 18th birthday first.
Driver licenses issued to non-immigrants are valid only through their authorized presence date in the United States, not to exceed one year.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Commercial Learner's Permit (EO03)
entries.summary: Requirements and procedures for obtaining a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) in Florida, including age requirements, exam prerequisites, issuance periods, endorsements, restrictions, and fees.

keyFacts.claim: A Commercial Learner's Permit must be held by all applicants before a CDL may be issued or upgraded, except for CDL upgrades that do not require new skill tests.
The minimum age to hold a CLP or CDL is 18 years of age, and customers aged 18, 19, and 20 are restricted to 'Intrastate Only' and prohibited from obtaining a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CLP must be held for at least 14 calendar days before the CDL Skills Test is permitted.
A CLP is issued for no more than 365 days from the date of issuance, not to exceed one year from the CDL General Knowledge pass date.
Commercial Learner's Permits require a licensed accompanying driver 21 years of age or older who holds a CDL license equivalent to or higher than the type of vehicle indicated on the permit.
Customers applying for a CLP must have a social security number and must self-certify and provide a current Medical Examiner's Certificate if required.

entries.title: Commercial Driver License (EO04)
entries.summary: Requirements, procedures, and fees for obtaining, renewing, upgrading, or replacing a Commercial Driver License (CDL) in Florida, including age requirements, residency proof, English proficiency, temporary permits, and endorsement fees.

keyFacts.claim: The minimum age to hold a Commercial Learner's Permit or CDL is 18 years of age.
Customers aged 18, 19, and 20 are restricted to intrastate only and are prohibited from obtaining a hazardous materials endorsement.
All CDL knowledge exams must be taken in English and applicants may not use an interpreter for CDL knowledge exams.
CDL applicants must be Florida residents and provide specific proof of Florida residency such as a Florida driver license held for more than six months or a Florida voter registration card.
Commercial Learner's Permits must be held at least 14 days before the Commercial Driver License skills test may be taken.
School employees who are required to hold a CDL pay a reduced fee of $48.00 instead of the standard $75.00 fee.

entries.title: Motorcycle Operation (EO05)
entries.summary: Requirements for motorcycle endorsements including age minimums (16+), mandatory safety course completion, fees ($7 endorsement + $6.25 service), helmet/eye protection rules, and differences between motorcycle-only vs motorcycle-also licenses.

keyFacts.claim: The minimum age to hold a motorcycle endorsed driver license is 16 years of age.
Florida law requires every first-time applicant for licensure to operate a motorcycle to provide proof of completion of a motorcycle safety course.
Customers under 18 are required to hold a Learner's License for at least 12 months or until their 18th birthday prior to issuance of motorcycle endorsement.
The motorcycle safety course completion is valid for one year from the course completion date, after which customers must retake the course.
Anyone 16 years of age but less than 21 years of age must wear a DOT approved helmet when operating or riding upon a motorcycle.

A driver license is not required to operate a bicycle with an electric helper motor not capable of propelling the bicycle faster than 20 miles per hour, providing the person is at least 16 years of age.

entries.title: Miscellaneous Transactions (EO06)
entries.summary: Covers various transactions that don't require card issuance: exam-only testing, driving record transcripts, voluntary contributions to charities, sanction clearances, document scanning, employee badges, and public records requests with associated fees.

keyFacts.claim: Exam-only transactions allow customers to take written tests without receiving a credential immediately.
Clearance transactions process sanction reinstatements when no new card will be issued.
Driving record transcripts are available for 3-year ($8.00), 7-year ($10.00), or certified records ($10.00).
Customers can make voluntary contributions to 21 authorized charitable organizations during any transaction.
FDLE letters can be issued to sexual offenders/predators who lack required documents, legal presence proof, or payment for a regular credential.

entries.title: Quick Links (HP01)
entries.summary: Provides overview of commonly accessed resources and tools available to customers, including emergency contact information services, forms, and reference materials for driver license and identification services.

keyFacts.claim: The Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles is charged with the orderly administration of Chapter 322, Florida Statutes.
Emergency Contact Information is a service that permits customers to provide contact information to a FLHSMV database for use by law enforcement in emergencies.
The Driver License Operations Manual is designed to aid in the issuance of driver licenses, identification cards, and other driver related services.
DAVID provides web-based access to driver license identity information, transactions, records, and vehicle titles and registrations.

entries.title: Alerts (HP02)
entries.summary: Describes the alert system that notifies staff of technical advisories, information notices, policy changes, and procedural updates that may affect driver license services and operations.

keyFacts.claim: The department is charged with the orderly administration of Chapter 322, Florida Statutes under legislative intent.
Changes in legislation or procedural changes approved by FLHSMV are communicated to staff through alerts.
Technical advisories are documents prepared by subject matter experts that provide detailed information to credentialing personnel.
Information notices provide general information to staff regarding driver license operations.
Alert action designations include immediate action types, action required, informational, software/web updates, and advisory categories.

entries.title: Address Requirements (IR01)
entries.summary: Rules for proving Florida residential address when getting or changing address on driver licenses and ID cards. Covers required documents, homeless situations, address exceptions for law enforcement/victims, and fees for address changes.

keyFacts.claim: Two different proofs of Florida residential address are required for Class E licenses and ID cards, each from a different source.
Utility bills, bank statements, and government documents must be dated within the last 60 days to be acceptable as address proof.
CDL and CLP holders must provide two documents from List A or one from List A and one from List B, with stricter requirements than Class E licenses.
Homeless customers can use General Delivery as their address with a Certification of Address form and letter from a shelter or agency.
Law enforcement officers, domestic violence victims, and certain public officials can qualify for address exceptions to protect their residential address.
Address changes must be completed within 30 days of moving and require a new credential to be issued.

entries.title: Application Question Requirements (IR02)
entries.summary: Details all questions asked during driver license, CDL, and ID card applications, including medical screening, voter registration, organ donation, veteran designation, and required responses that affect eligibility or processing.

keyFacts.claim: Customers must swear under penalty of perjury that application information is true and correct, and selecting 'Cancel' terminates the transaction.
Customers with epilepsy, fainting, or dizzy spells within the last two years may receive only a 60-day temporary permit pending medical review.
Customers with two DUI convictions in five years or three in ten years must provide proof of Florida liability insurance and DUI course completion.
Customers can choose to register as organ donors and have the designation printed on their credential.
Honorably discharged veterans can request veteran designation on their credential and contact information for federal and state benefits.
Tax Collector Service Fee is $6.25 for driver license application processing.

entries.title: Card Designations (IR03)
entries.summary: Rules for adding special designations to driver licenses and ID cards, including veteran, organ donor, deaf/hard of hearing, developmental disability, insulin dependent, FWC lifetime licenses, and REAL ID designations. Covers required documentation and fees.

keyFacts.claim: Deaf or hard of hearing designation can be added to any Florida credential at customer request with no proof required.
Developmental disability designation requires a physician-signed Application for Identification Card with Developmental Disability Designation form.
Veterans discharged under conditions other than dishonorable or uncharacterized can add veteran designation with DD214 or approved discharge document at no fee.
FWC lifetime license designations require presentation of physical FWC lifetime license card.
REAL ID star designation is automatically added when customer meets document requirements for proof of identification, residential address, and social security number.
Organ donor and insulin dependent designations can be added at customer request with no extra fee and no documentation required.

feeAmounts.label: Deaf/Hard of Hearing designation with other credential changes
Deaf/Hard of Hearing designation replacement only
FWC lifetime designations with other credential changes

entries.title: Certification of Driving Experience of a Minor (IR04)
entries.summary: Requirements for minors under 18 getting a Class E or Motorcycle Only license, including 12-month learner's permit holding period, 50-hour driving experience certification by parent/guardian, and fees for license upgrades.

keyFacts.claim: Customers under 18 must hold a learner's license for at least 12 months with no moving traffic convictions before obtaining a Class E or Motorcycle Only license.
A parent, guardian or responsible adult must certify that the minor has completed a minimum of 50 hours behind the wheel driving experience, with at least 10 hours at night.
The customer may have one moving traffic conviction within 12 months from the learner's license issue date if adjudication is withheld.
Minor customers with an out-of-state Class E license or equivalent are not required to have parental certification of driving experience.
Minor customers with an out-of-state learner's license applying for a Florida Class E license are required to have parental certification of driving experience.

feeAmounts.label: Learner's License / Class E Driver License
Learner's License Upgrade (with changes to the card)

entries.title: Medical Examiner Certificate (IR05)
entries.summary: Requirements for CDL holders to maintain medical examiner certificates, including four self-certification categories (A-D), medical variance restrictions, and disqualification consequences for non-compliance.

keyFacts.claim: CDL applicants must self-certify in one of four categories (A-D) based on interstate/intrastate commerce and medical certification requirements.
Categories A (Non-excepted Interstate) and C (Non-excepted Intrastate) require maintaining a valid Medical Examiner's Certificate.
Categories B (Excepted Interstate) and D (Excepted Intrastate) do not require medical certification for specific exempt operations like government driving or emergency operations.
Medical examiner certificates are now electronically verified through FMCSA and no longer need to be physically presented.
Failure to maintain current medical certification results in CDL disqualification with a $75 fee plus $6.25 service fee.

feeAmounts.label: Disqualification for Failure to Comply with CDL Medical Self-Certification

entries.title: Commercial Driver License Waivers (IR06)
entries.summary: Requirements and procedures for CDL waivers when customers don't meet physical requirements due to missing extremities, vision issues, or diabetes. Covers federal vs state waiver contact information and associated fees.

keyFacts.claim: Customers with missing extremities must present a limb waiver to obtain a CDL, either intrastate or interstate.
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration no longer issues vision waivers, instead medical providers can issue medical cards directly if requirements are met.
Florida Statutes Section 316.302(2)(i) provides an intrastate CDL exemption for drivers with monocular vision without requiring a paper waiver.
Federal diabetes waivers are no longer issued, with medical providers now handling certification directly through updated procedures.
CDL holders operating government commercial motor vehicles are exempt from limb waiver requirements.

entries.title: Endorsements (IR07)
entries.summary: Requirements, exams, and fees for driver license endorsements including motorcycle, CDL endorsements (hazardous materials, passenger, school bus, tank vehicle, double/triple trailers). Covers eligibility, background checks, and application processes.

keyFacts.claim: Hazardous materials endorsements require U.S. citizenship or permanent legal residence, fingerprinting, and TSA background check.
HazMat knowledge exam results are valid for 60 days from the exam pass date and must be completed before the CDL transaction.
School bus endorsement requires both passenger endorsement and school bus endorsement knowledge exams plus skills testing in a school bus.
Motorcycle endorsements are required for operating vehicles with engine size more than 50cc, available as 'Also' or 'Only' options.
CDL endorsements can only be added or removed during the issuance process at credentialing services offices.

entries.title: Sex Requirements (IR08)
entries.summary: Establishes requirements for sex designation on Florida driver licenses and ID cards. Sex must be male or female based on primary identification documents and cannot be changed from biological sex. Includes fees for original and replacement credentials.

keyFacts.claim: Customer's sex is taken from the primary identification document for credential issuance and must be male (M) or female (F).
If a birth certificate or US passport shows nonbinary X for sex and no other primary documentation indicates sex, the customer must specify which sex they were born with.
The customer's sex may not be changed on the Florida credential to differ from their biological sex.
Florida statutes require proof of gender/sex along with legal name, lawful presence, social security number, and two forms of residential address.

entries.title: Identity & Legal Presence (IR09)
entries.summary: Requirements for proving identity and legal presence when applying for Florida driver licenses and ID cards. Covers acceptable documents for U.S. citizens, immigrants, non-immigrants, and Canadian citizens, plus secondary identification requirements.

keyFacts.claim: All customers applying for Florida credentials must provide proof of identity and U.S. citizenship or legal presence using original or certified copies of documents.
U.S. citizens can establish identity and citizenship with a U.S. birth certificate, valid U.S. passport, Certificate of Naturalization, or Certificate of Citizenship.
Puerto Rico birth certificates must be issued July 1, 2010 or later to be accepted for Florida credential issuance.
Non-immigrants must provide both proof of identity/legal presence and secondary identification, and their credentials will display 'TEMPORARY'.
Canadian citizens can be issued credentials valid for up to six months using proof of Canadian citizenship, or longer periods with USCIS documents.
Customers must obtain a replacement credential within 30 days of changing citizenship status and pay the applicable replacement fee.

entries.title: Inmate Re-entry Requirements (IR10)
entries.summary: Special no-fee ID cards and replacement driver licenses available to inmates through mobile FLOW units only. Department of Corrections inmates must be released within 12 months and not possess valid FL credentials. Cannot be processed at regular service centers.

keyFacts.claim: Inmates can receive no-fee Florida ID cards or replacement driver licenses within 6 months before release from Department of Corrections custody.
No-fee inmate transactions can only be processed by Florida Licensing on Wheels (FLOW) mobile units, not at regular field offices or tax collector locations.
Department of Corrections inmates are eligible for no-fee issuance only if they don't have a valid Florida credential and are scheduled for release within 12 months.
Inmates with open driver license sanctions may receive a no-fee ID card but must clear all sanctions before driving privileges are restored.
Department of Juvenile Justice offenders in custody or under supervision are eligible for no-fee original, replacement, or renewal ID cards.

entries.title: Motor Voter Registration (IR11)
entries.summary: Requirements and process for voter registration during driver license and ID card transactions. Customers 16+ who are US citizens and Florida residents can register to vote or update voter registration, with opt-out available.

keyFacts.claim: Every driver license or ID card application automatically serves as a voter registration application unless the customer opts out.
Customers must be US citizens, Florida residents, and at least 16 years old to apply for voter registration (18 to actually vote).
Customers cannot register to vote if they have been adjudicated mentally incapacitated with respect to voting or convicted of a felony, unless their rights have been restored.
Customers can choose to register as a new voter, update existing registration, or request a replacement voter information card.
The tax collector cannot charge the $6.25 service fee for processing mailed or hand-delivered voter registration applications.

entries.title: Name Requirements (IR12)
entries.summary: Requirements for names on Florida driver licenses and ID cards, including acceptable name change documents (marriage certificates, court orders, divorce decrees), name formatting rules, and procedures for U.S. citizens vs. immigrants/non-immigrants.

keyFacts.claim: Florida law requires the customer's full name (first, middle or maiden, and last) appear on a Florida credential.
U.S. citizens' names are entered exactly as listed on their primary identification, with name changes requiring approved name change documents.
Marriage certificates must be original or certified copies of government marriage certificates with appropriate seals from the issuing agency.
Immigrants and non-immigrants must change their name on USCIS documents before their name can be changed on Florida credentials.
Suffixes like SR, JR, I, II, III can be added or deleted at customer request without requiring identification.
Name corrections due to examiner/agent error on REAL ID compliant cards qualify for no-fee replacement credentials.

entries.title: Organ and Tissue Donation (IR13)
entries.summary: Rules for organ and tissue donor registration during driver license and ID card transactions, including enrollment process, donor designation display on cards, withdrawal procedures, and associated fees.

keyFacts.claim: Customers are asked during all driver license and ID transactions if they want to register as an organ donor.
Customers can choose to register as an organ donor but not have it printed on their card.
Customers can designate their specific organ and tissue donation choices online at www.DonateLifeFlorida.org.
Minors can register as organ donors online, but final donation decisions fall to their legal guardians.
Organ donor withdrawals can be processed online at www.DonateLifeFlorida.org to save an office visit.
A replacement license or ID must be issued to remove the organ donor designation from the physical card.

feeAmounts.label: Replacement to add or remove organ donor designation only

entries.title: Parental Consent (IR14)
entries.summary: Requirements for parental consent when minors under 18 apply for driver licenses, including who can sign consent forms, when consent can be waived for married or emancipated minors, and how consent can be withdrawn.

keyFacts.claim: Persons under 18 applying for a driver license must have parental consent from a father, mother, guardian, or other responsible adult.
The parental consent form must be notarized or signed in the presence of credentialing personnel at the office.
Foster parents, group home representatives, caseworkers, or guardians ad litem can sign consent for minors in foster care without assuming liability.
Parental consent is waived if the minor presents an original or certified copy of their marriage certificate or emancipation court order.
The person who signed parental consent can withdraw it at any time through MyDMV Portal or written request, which will cancel the minor's license.

entries.title: REAL ID (IR15)
entries.summary: REAL ID requirements for Florida driver licenses and ID cards, including compliance standards, required documents (primary ID, social security proof, address proof), federal facility access deadlines, and card identifiers with gold stars.

keyFacts.claim: All customers must provide primary identification/legal presence, proof of social security number, and proof of residential address for REAL ID compliance.
After U.S. citizens and immigrants establish material compliance, they are not required to present primary identification for subsequent transactions.
Non-immigrants are required to provide primary identification/legal presence for every driver license or ID card issuance.
REAL ID will be required for boarding federally regulated commercial aircraft starting May 7, 2025.
REAL ID compliant credentials are marked with a gold star in the top right corner of the card.

entries.title: Restrictions (IR16)
entries.summary: Rules for driver license restrictions including corrective lenses, automatic transmission, power steering, daylight only, business purposes, ignition interlock, and CDL restrictions. Covers when restrictions are required, who can add/remove them, and testing requirements.

keyFacts.claim: Corrective lenses restriction is imposed when the customer requires contact lenses or glasses to meet vision requirements.
Business purposes restriction allows driving for work, education, church, and medical purposes but cannot be added to a Commercial Driver License.
Daylight only restriction can only be added or removed by eye specialists using Form HSMV 72010 and is never imposed at credentialing personnel discretion.
CDL customers with automatic transmission restriction must obtain a Commercial Learner's Permit and hold it 14 days before taking skills test in manual transmission vehicle to remove restriction.
Ignition interlock restriction limits driver to vehicles equipped with ignition interlock device and requires court authorization to remove.

entries.title: Scanning Requirements (IR17)
entries.summary: Specifies which documents must be scanned during driver license transactions, including identification documents, proof of address, court orders, and immigration papers. Medical documents cannot be scanned. Includes $6.25 Tax Collector service fee if applicable.

keyFacts.claim: All documents used as part of a transaction that do not contain medical information must be scanned into the customer's record.
Medical documents like Report of Eye Exam Form HSMV 72010 and Mature Driver Vision Test Form HSMV 72119 should not be scanned.
All documents submitted as proof of address must be scanned, including the Certification of Address form and supporting documents in the certifier's name.
Envelopes are not admissible for proof of residential address, but the document inside can be scanned with permission.
Both front and back sides must be scanned for certain documents including out-of-state licenses, passports, and immigration documents.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Selective Service (IR18)
entries.summary: Males aged 18-25 must consent to Selective Service registration when applying for or renewing driver licenses, learner permits, commercial licenses, or ID cards. Refusal to consent terminates the application.

keyFacts.claim: Males aged 18-25 (US citizens or immigrants) must consent to Selective Service registration when applying for driver licenses, learner permits, commercial licenses, or ID cards.
Males under 18 will be required to register with Selective Service when they turn 18 as required by federal law.
If a customer refuses Selective Service registration consent, the application must be terminated.
Proof of Selective Service compliance will be printed on the customer's receipt.
Customers with Selective Service questions should contact the Selective Service System website or call 1-888-655-6888.

entries.title: Sexual Offender / Sexual Predator / Career Offender (IR19)
entries.summary: Requirements for sexual offenders, sexual predators, and career offenders to register at driver license offices and obtain credentials with special identifiers. Covers registration forms, card markings, and procedures for those unable to obtain credentials.

keyFacts.claim: Sexual offenders, sexual predators, and career offenders who are not incarcerated must register in person at a driver license or tax collector office and present proof of registration from the local sheriff's department or Department of Corrections.
Sexual offenders will have '943.0435 F.S.' printed on the front of their credential, while sexual predators will have 'SEXUAL PREDATOR' printed on the front.
Out-of-state registration forms cannot be used - customers must register with the sheriff's office in their Florida county of residence to obtain proper paperwork.
Sexual offender and sexual predator identifiers will not print on credentials processed through the Central Issuance Processing System and require a return visit for a no-fee issuance.
Customers unable to obtain a credential due to missing documents or fees can receive an FDLE letter to document their registration while gathering required materials.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Social Security Requirements (IR20)
entries.summary: Social Security number requirements for driver licenses and ID cards, including acceptable proof documents, verification process, and special rules for non-immigrants and work authorization status.

keyFacts.claim: All driver license and ID card applicants must provide proof of Social Security number or demonstrate ineligibility for a SSN.
Acceptable proof of SSN includes Social Security card, W-2 forms, 1099 forms, pay stubs, or self-certification form HSMV 71330.
Non-immigrants with work-authorized status must provide proof of SSN or a letter of ineligibility from the Social Security Administration.
F1 and M1 student visa holders are considered work-authorized and must provide SSN proof or obtain an ineligibility letter through their sponsor school.
Social Security numbers are verified online with the SSA before credential issuance, and it may take up to 48 hours for SSA records to update.

entries.title: Veterans (IR21)
entries.summary: Requirements for veteran designation on driver licenses/ID cards, fee waivers for 100% disabled veterans, acceptable discharge documents, and proof of veteran status for benefits eligibility.

keyFacts.claim: Veterans discharged under conditions other than dishonorable or uncharacterized may add a Veteran designation to their Florida driver license or ID card.
100% disabled veterans receive fee waivers for most driver license transactions including renewals, replacements, and reinstatement fees.
DD Form 214 and various other military discharge documents are acceptable proof of veteran status for the designation.
Adding only the Veteran designation to an existing credential is processed at no fee.
Temporary 100% disability ratings do not qualify veterans for fee waivers, only permanent ratings are eligible.

feeAmounts.label: Original or Renewal of Class E or Motorcycle only DL
Original, Renewal or Replacement ID card

entries.title: Voluntary Contributions (IR22)
entries.summary: Rules for optional charitable donations during driver license and ID card transactions. Customers can donate $1 or more to 21 approved organizations. Tax collector charges $6.25 service fee for processing donations.

keyFacts.claim: Customers can make voluntary donations to 21 approved charitable organizations during driver license or ID card transactions.
Voluntary contributions must be $1.00 or more per organization.
The tax collector charges a $6.25 service fee for processing voluntary contributions.
Customers without a Florida driver license or ID card can still make voluntary contributions using a special record number.
Approved organizations include Autism Services, Best Buddies International, Disabled American Veterans, and 18 other charities.

entries.title: Unclaimed/Abandoned Property (MP01)
entries.summary: Explains unclaimed property notices that may appear on driver license records, contact information for claiming abandoned property through Florida Department of Financial Services, and applicable service fees.

keyFacts.claim: Unclaimed property notices may appear on Florida driver license or ID card holder records when they have abandoned property.
Unclaimed property includes dormant bank accounts, uncashed checks, insurance proceeds, stocks, dividends, deposits, and credit balances.
Property is considered unclaimed after being held by businesses or government entities for a set period, usually five years.
Customers can contact the Florida Department of Financial Services Bureau of Unclaimed Property at (850) 413-2253 to claim their property.
A tax collector service fee of $6.25 may apply when processing unclaimed property inquiries.

feeAmounts.label: Tax Collector Service Fee if applicable

entries.title: Autonomous Vehicles (MP02)
entries.summary: Defines autonomous vehicle types and requirements. Fully autonomous vehicles don't need human operators. Non-fully autonomous vehicles must alert human operators of system failures and meet federal safety standards.

keyFacts.claim: A licensed human operator is not required to operate a fully autonomous vehicle.
Autonomous vehicles registered in Florida must be certified in accordance with federal regulations when required by federal law.
Autonomous vehicles must be capable of being operated in compliance with Florida traffic and motor vehicle laws regardless of whether the automated driving system is engaged.
Non-fully autonomous vehicles must have a system to safely alert a licensed human operator if an automated driving system failure is detected.
When an alert is given in a non-fully autonomous vehicle, the system must require the human operator to take control or achieve a minimal risk condition.

entries.title: Blocked Records (MP03)
entries.summary: Explains privacy protections for driver license and vehicle records under federal law, plus special address blocking available to law enforcement, judges, and other eligible public officials and their families.

keyFacts.claim: Personal information including name, address, driver license number, date of birth, social security number, and photograph is automatically blocked in all driver license and motor vehicle records.
Customers must request an unblocked record if they need their personal information provided on their driving record.
Current or former law enforcement personnel, judges, state attorneys, firefighters, and their spouses, children or dependents are eligible for enhanced record blocking protection.
Eligible public officials can have their mailing address printed on their credential instead of their residential address by submitting Form HSMV96020.
To make address blocking permanent, customers must mail the completed form and eligibility documentation to the department after their transaction.

entries.title: Card Issuance Method (MP04)
entries.summary: Explains how driver licenses and ID cards are issued - either over the counter immediately for verified customers, or by mail from central processing for unverified applications with a 60-day temporary permit issued.

keyFacts.claim: Customers who verify in the Verification of Lawful Status system receive their credential immediately over the counter.
When customer status cannot be verified, a 60-day temporary permit is issued and the permanent card is mailed from Tallahassee if verification is later successful.
If application information cannot be verified during central processing, customers receive a cancellation letter requesting proper documents or data correction.
Card issuance is denied when personnel suspect or determine presented documents are fraudulent or altered.

entries.title: Crash Reports (MP05)
entries.summary: Rules for obtaining Florida traffic crash reports, including self-reporting requirements within 10 days, 60-day confidentiality period, online purchase options at $10 per report, and mail/in-person request procedures with required sworn statements.

keyFacts.claim: Drivers involved in crashes with property damage that don't require law enforcement reports must submit a self-report to FLHSMV within 10 days.
Traffic crash reports are confidential for 60 days after filing, except for parties involved in the crash and other specific exempted parties.
Crash reports can be purchased online for $10.00 each plus a $2.00 convenience fee, with a maximum of 10 reports per transaction.
Customers requesting crash reports within the 60-day confidentiality period must complete a sworn statement and meet specific exemption requirements.
Purchased crash reports must be downloaded within 48 hours and become available immediately after online purchase.

entries.title: Combine Records (MP06)
entries.summary: Procedures for requesting the combination of duplicate driver license records when multiple records exist for the same person in the DHSMV system.

keyFacts.claim: When two or more records exist for the same customer, a request must be made to combine these records.
Record combination requests are submitted using the Combine Records Request form accessed through PartnerNet.
All fields on the Combine Records Request form must be completed before submission.
The combine records request is submitted via email with the form information attached.
Additional comments can be added to the combine records request email if needed.

entries.title: Convenience Transactions (MP07)
entries.summary: Rules for online, mail-in, and military extension options for driver license and ID card renewals and replacements. Covers eligibility requirements, fees, and processes for convenient alternatives to in-person visits.

keyFacts.claim: Online and mail-in renewals are available for US citizens and immigrants with established status on record who are Real-ID compliant.
Mail-in renewals are only available every other renewal period - two consecutive convenience renewals are not permitted.
Customers 80 and over must provide a vision test to use convenience renewal methods.
Active-duty military members and dependents can get free extensions for Class E licenses while stationed outside Florida.
Military extensions are valid until 90 days after discharge or return to Florida and require military orders as proof.

feeAmounts.label: Class E/CDL Driver License Replacement Fee

entries.title: Fees (MP08)
entries.summary: Complete fee schedule for Florida driver licenses, ID cards, and CDLs including original issuance, renewals, replacements, designations, reinstatements, and exams. Also covers no-fee situations like veteran benefits, defective cards, and financial hardship.

keyFacts.claim: Class E driver licenses cost $48.00 for original issuance and renewals.
Commercial driver licenses cost $75.00, but school employees pay only $48.00 with proper employment documentation.
Delinquent renewals within one year of expiration incur a $15.00 late fee, which can be waived by passing the complete Class E knowledge exam.
Most replacement transactions (address change, name change, lost card) cost $25.00.
Veterans receive no-fee replacements when adding veteran designation and must present DD Form 214 or VA identification.
Defective cards, examiner errors, and stolen cards with police reports qualify for no-fee replacements.

entries.title: Fraud (Driver License & ID Card) (MP09)
entries.summary: Procedures for reporting driver license and ID card fraud, fraud investigations, possible imposter flags, fraud suspensions/cancellations, and associated reinstatement fees.

keyFacts.claim: Customers can request a 'Possible Imposter' flag be added to their driving record to prevent online transactions and require in-person visits with at least two identification documents.
The Possible Imposter flag prevents online transactions involving credential issuance and requires customers to report in person with at least two identification documents.
Customers with a Possible Imposter flag must prove identity at every issuance, requiring at least two documents with at least one being primary identification.
Driver license fraud results in a one-year suspension, while ID card fraud results in cancellation of the ID card.
A fraud suspension reinstatement fee of $45.00 is required for every fraud suspension.

entries.title: International Driving Permit (MP10)
entries.summary: Explains International Driving Permits (IDPs) for US residents traveling abroad and foreign visitors driving in Florida. Covers who can issue IDPs, validity requirements, and that Florida doesn't require foreign license holders to have an IDP while driving in Florida.

keyFacts.claim: Florida law does not require a customer holding a valid foreign driver license to hold an International Driving Permit while driving in Florida.
An International Driving Permit cannot be used as proof of identity.
Only the American Automobile Association and American Automobile Touring Alliance are authorized to issue International Driving Permits to U.S. residents.
International Driving Permits are only available to people who are at least 18 years old and have a valid driver's license issued by a U.S. state or territory.
An International Driving Permit is valid for one year from the date of issue, provided the home country's driver license is also valid for that entire year.
The International Driving Permit is not valid without the accompanying home country's license.

feeAmounts.label: Tax collector service fee if applicable

entries.title: Issuance Periods (MP11)
entries.summary: Specifies validity periods for ID cards, driver licenses, and CDLs based on age and immigration status. Covers temporary permit eligibility for REAL ID compliance, vision issues, medical reviews, and driving test failures.

keyFacts.claim: ID cards for customers age 5-14 are valid for four years, while those 15 and older receive eight-year validity.
Non-immigrant ID cards and driver licenses are issued only through the date they are legally entitled to be present in the United States, not exceeding one year for ID cards.
Customers can receive a 60-day temporary permit if they cannot provide REAL ID compliance documents and their current license is valid or expired 60 days or less.
Driver licenses for customers 79 and under are valid for eight years, while those 80 and older receive six-year validity.
Commercial Learner's Permits are valid for one year with no renewal option.
Hazardous Material Endorsed CDLs are valid for four years and only issued to U.S. Citizens and Permanent residents.

entries.title: License/ID Not Received from CIPS (MP12)
entries.summary: Procedures for customers who didn't receive their driver license or ID card in the mail within 60 days, including replacement options, fees, and requirements for address changes or mail-in/online transactions.

keyFacts.claim: Customers should receive their card within 60 days of the transaction date at the driver license or tax collector office.
If a card was not returned to FLHSMV and more than 14 days have passed since printing, customers receive a no-fee replacement if their address is the same.
Customers are charged a $25.00 replacement fee if their address is different from the address on the card that was returned to FLHSMV.
If it takes six months or more before the customer requests a new card, they will be charged the $25.00 replacement fee.
For mail-in/online transactions, if the customer's address has changed, they are charged the $25.00 replacement fee plus $6.25 tax collector service fee if processed at a tax collector office.
