entries.title: Low Speed/Slow Moving Vehicles and Golf Carts (MP13)
entries.summary: Rules for operating golf carts and low-speed vehicles on public roads, including age requirements, licensing needs, equipment requirements, speed limits, and where these vehicles can legally be driven.

keyFacts.claim: Anyone under 18 operating a golf cart on public roads must possess a valid learner's permit or driver license.
Persons 18 or older operating golf carts on public roads must have valid government-issued photo identification.
Low-speed vehicles must be registered, insured, and titled, and operators must have a valid driver's license.
Golf carts may only operate on state roads with posted speed limits of 30 mph or less.
Low-speed vehicles may only operate on streets with posted speed limits of 35 mph or less.
Golf carts may only be operated between sunrise and sunset unless local government allows extended hours with additional equipment.

entries.title: Persons Exempt from Obtaining a Florida Driver License (MP14)
entries.summary: Lists specific categories of people who are exempt from needing a Florida driver license, including active military members and their families, federal employees, non-residents with valid out-of-state licenses, students, and others.

keyFacts.claim: Active duty U.S. Armed Forces members, their spouses, and dependents living with them are exempt from obtaining a Florida driver license if they hold a valid out-of-state license, learner's permit, or U.S. Armed Forces driving permit.
U.S. Government employees operating non-commercial vehicles owned or leased by the federal government for official business are exempt from Florida driver license requirements.
Non-residents at least 16 years old with a valid non-commercial license from their home state or country may operate a Class E vehicle in Florida without a Florida license.
Non-resident full-time students enrolled in any institute of higher learning are exempt from obtaining a Florida driver license.
Persons working for firms under contract to the U.S. government are exempt from Florida driver license requirements for 60 days.

entries.title: Persons Required to Obtain Florida License (MP15)
entries.summary: Defines who must obtain a Florida driver license and when, including residents within 30 days of residency, non-residents within 30 days of employment/school enrollment, and military exemptions for active duty personnel with valid out-of-state licenses.

keyFacts.claim: Florida residents who want to operate a motor vehicle must obtain a Florida driver license within 30 days of becoming a resident.
Non-residents must obtain a Florida driver license within 30 days of accepting employment in Florida.
Non-residents must obtain a Florida driver license within 30 days of engaging in any trade, profession or occupation in Florida.
Non-residents must obtain a Florida driver license within 30 days of entering their children in Florida public schools.

Active duty U.S. Armed Forces members, their spouses, and dependents are exempt from obtaining a Florida driver license if they hold a valid out-of-state license, learner's permit, or U.S. Armed Forces driving permit.

entries.title: Photographs - Video - Audio Recordings (MP16)
entries.summary: Rules for taking photographs, videos, or audio recordings in driver license offices. Covers what areas allow recording, restrictions in testing areas, and policies for driving skills tests and exam materials.

keyFacts.claim: The public may take photographs, videos, or audio recordings in public areas of driver license offices as long as they don't capture other customers' private information.
Photographs, videos, or audio recordings are not allowed in testing or screening areas to protect customer privacy and prevent disruption.
Exam questions and answer sheets cannot be copied or videotaped, though customers may review their own completed exams.
Customers taking a driving skills test cannot take photographs, videos, or audio recordings during the test, and dashcams must be turned off or removed.
Observers may take photographs or videos of driving tests from a safe distance as long as they don't interfere with the test.

entries.title: Public Records Request (MP17)
entries.summary: Explains how to request copies of driver license, vehicle registration, title, and other motor vehicle records. Covers privacy protections, fees for copies, and contact information for different types of record requests.

keyFacts.claim: Personal information including Social Security Number, Driver License Number, name, address, phone number, medical information, photos, and emergency contact information is protected and automatically blocked in motor vehicle records.
Public records requests do not require the requestor to identify themselves, show ID, or explain why they want the information.
Driver license, tag, title, registration, and crash statistics records requests are handled by the Division of Motorist Services Bureau of Records in Tallahassee.
Record inspection has no fee, but photocopies cost $0.50 per page and certified copies cost $1.00 per page.
Driver history transcripts cost $8.00 for three-year records, $10.00 for seven-year records, and $10.00 for certified three or seven-year records.

entries.title: Retention of Previously Held Credentials (MP18)
entries.summary: Rules for surrendering out-of-state, Florida, or foreign credentials when getting a new Florida driver license or ID card. Covers what happens to your old credential and special rules for Canadian licenses.

keyFacts.claim: You must surrender any valid out-of-state credential before a Florida credential can be issued.
If your out-of-state credential was lost or stolen, you can provide a statement instead of surrendering the physical card.
Out-of-country licenses (except Canadian) are returned to you without any modifications.
Canadian license holders can keep their Canadian license if they take the complete Florida examination.
Canadian license holders who surrender their license only need to take the vision exam and can receive their old license back with a corner cut off.

entries.title: Safe Driver Designation (MP19)
entries.summary: Explains eligibility for Safe Driver status on driver license renewals, requiring no convictions in past 3 years and no suspensions/revocations in past 7 years. Lists non-moving violations that don't disqualify you.

keyFacts.claim: Safe Driver status is awarded upon driver license renewal if you have no convictions in the past three years.
Safe Driver status requires no suspensions, revocations, or disqualifications within the past seven years.
Failure to exhibit vehicle registration does not count against Safe Driver status.
Failure to carry or exhibit a driver license does not disqualify you from Safe Driver status.
Operating with a license expired for six months or less does not affect Safe Driver eligibility.
Failure to notify the department of address or name changes within 30 days does not count against Safe Driver status.

entries.title: Termination (MP20)
entries.summary: Rules for surrendering Florida driver licenses and ID cards when applying for the other credential, moving out-of-state, or seeking jury duty exemption. Covers eligibility requirements and processes when returning to Florida.

keyFacts.claim: Florida law prohibits holding both a Florida driver license and ID card - you must choose which credential to retain when applying for replacement or renewal.
When you apply for a Florida ID card while holding a Florida driver license, your driver license will be terminated.
When you apply for a Florida driver license while holding a Florida ID card, your ID card will be terminated.
If you surrendered your Florida license out-of-state and return within 12 months, you may be eligible for renewal rather than original issuance.
Customers with sanctioned Florida driver licenses may be eligible for an ID card, which cancels the driver license but keeps the same expiration date.

entries.title: Transcript Sales (MP21)
entries.summary: Rules for obtaining Florida driving record transcripts, including types (3-year, 7-year, complete), certification options, where to purchase (tax collector, online, mail), fees, and how to correct errors on driving records.

keyFacts.claim: Three-year driving records cost $8.00 non-certified or $10.00 certified and are the most common type needed for insurance and employment.
Seven-year and complete driving records each cost $10.00 whether certified or non-certified.
Driving records can be obtained at tax collector offices, through MyDMV Portal, by mail to Bureau of Records, or from some Clerk of Court offices.
Tax collector offices charge an additional $6.25 service fee on top of the transcript fee.
Transcript sales are final and may not be returned for a refund, and reprints must be completed the same day as the sale.
To correct errors on driving records, customers should contact the Clerk of Circuit Court where the violation occurred for citation disputes.

entries.title: Valid in Florida Only (MP22)
entries.summary: Explains that Valid in Florida Only (VFO) driver licenses are no longer issued in Florida. Customers with old VFO licenses must be informed this designation is no longer available and they cannot obtain new VFO licenses.

keyFacts.claim: Valid in Florida Only (VFO) driver licenses are no longer issued in Florida.
VFO licenses were previously available only for non-commercial licenses, not commercial motor vehicle licenses.
Prior to November 1, 2009, VFO licenses were issued to people who needed to retain out-of-state licenses due to part-time residence or employment.
Customers with old Florida driver licenses bearing the VFO designation must be informed that VFO is no longer an option.
Current Florida law has no provisions that permit issuing VFO driver licenses.

entries.title: Back Up Issuance Procedures (MP23)
entries.summary: Explains what happens when verification systems are offline, including temporary permits, delayed processing, and restrictions on certain license types like CDL and CLP when systems are unavailable.

keyFacts.claim: When Social Security verification is offline, transactions are processed but verified later through a nightly batch process.
If Social Security verification fails after processing, customers receive a notice and their record gets a pending cancellation.
When PDPS/NDR systems are offline, customers receive a 60-day temporary permit while verification is completed.
CDL and Commercial Learner's Permit transactions cannot be processed when SPEXS system is down and customers must return later.
Regular driver license renewals and replacements can still be issued with temporary permits when SPEXS is offline.
When lawful status verification is offline, credentials are processed but may require later review by the Document Validation Unit if verification fails.

entries.title: Fingerprinting Services (MP24)
entries.summary: Describes fingerprinting services available at driver license offices for FLHSMV employees, vendors, and Tax Collector employees. Covers required forms, identification, and processing procedures for background check compliance.

keyFacts.claim: Driver license offices with Livescan fingerprinting devices provide employee fingerprinting services for FLHSMV employees, vendors, and Tax Collector employees.
Anyone involved in REAL ID driver license production or CDL transactions must meet specific background check requirements through fingerprinting.
Three types of employee fingerprinting are available: FLHSMV Employee/Vendor (non CJIS), FHP/CJIS Employee/Vendor, and Tax Collector Employee.
Employees or vendors seeking fingerprinting must present a completed form with their name, signature, supervisor information, and a state-issued driver license or identification card.
If fingerprints are rejected by FDLE or FBI, employees may return for re-fingerprinting using a Transaction Control Reference (TCR) number to avoid additional billing.

entries.title: ID Go Solution (MP25)
entries.summary: Mobile ID card issuance service for customers physically unable to visit an office. Covers eligibility criteria, required documents, fees, and process for obtaining REAL ID compliant identification cards through the portable ID Go equipment.

keyFacts.claim: ID Go Solution is intended for individuals that are physically unable to go into a credentialing office.
The ID Go service must be available and applied consistently and uniformly throughout the county if offered by the Tax Collector.
All documents required as part of a transaction must be scanned, except for any documents indicating medical information.
Customers may be eligible for a no-fee 100% poverty level ID card with required eligibility documentation.
The transaction must be finalized and cashiered on the same date the transaction was started.

entries.title: Field Reports (RE01)
entries.summary: Describes daily transaction reports and end-of-day procedures for driver license offices, including cashier checkout processes, revenue deposits, and various transaction journals that track office productivity and fee collection.

keyFacts.claim: Transaction reports must be run daily and kept electronically or on paper for 13 months.
The Office Productivity Summary report provides details about time and productivity for each transaction processed.
The Transaction Detail Journal provides a list of all transactions, total transaction counts and fee breakout for revenue.
The Clear/Re-Open Activity report tracks all clearance transactions and whether clearance requirements were met prior to clearance.
The Change of Lawful Status report audits changes in citizenship status including Non-Immigrant, Immigrant, and US Citizen designations.

entries.title: Definitions (RS01)
entries.summary: Comprehensive definitions of terms used throughout driver license operations, including legal presence documents, vision requirements, commercial license classifications, insurance forms, and immigration status terminology.

keyFacts.claim: The Acceptable Documents Table (ADT) provides information on documents required to prove legal presence and is constantly revised.
A minimum binocular field of vision of 130 degrees is required to obtain a driver license, with normal binocular visual field being 180 degrees.
Class E License is required for non-commercial motor vehicles with GVWR less than 26,001 pounds, including passenger cars, 15 passenger vans, trucks, RVs, and mopeds 50cc or less.
Commercial Driver License Class A requires GCWR of 26,001+ pounds with towed unit(s) over 10,000 pounds GVWR.
FR-44 form certifies bodily injury and property damage liability coverage to comply with 100k/300k/50k requirements and remains in effect until replaced or terminated by FR-46.
Telescopic lenses are not permitted to meet Florida minimum vision requirements and customers wearing them must be issued a field revocation order for inadequate vision.

entries.title: Acronyms (RS02)
entries.summary: Reference guide listing acronyms and abbreviations used throughout driver license and motor vehicle operations, including terms for licenses, endorsements, testing, documentation, and regulatory agencies.

keyFacts.claim: CDL stands for Commercial Driver License and CLP stands for Commercial Learner's Permit.
REAL ID Act is abbreviated as RID or RIDA in driver license operations.
HAZMAT or HM refers to Hazardous Materials endorsements on commercial licenses.
DUI stands for Driving Under the Influence and DWLSR means Driving While License is Cancelled, Suspended, Revoked, or Disqualified.
TLSAE stands for Traffic Law Substance Abuse Education course required for certain license applications.

entries.title: Statute Cross Reference (RS03)
entries.summary: Comprehensive cross-reference of Florida Statutes and regulations that govern driver license operations, including requirements for licenses, renewals, suspensions, CDL operations, and various motor vehicle-related laws.

keyFacts.claim: Address changes must be reported within 30 days of moving as required by Section 322.19(2), Florida Statutes.
Canadian licenses are reciprocated under Section 322.12(1) and 322.18, Florida Statutes.
Commercial driver license holders cannot have out-of-state addresses per Section 322.03(3)(a), Florida Statutes.
Learner's license must be held for 12 months under Section 322.05(2)(a)(b), Florida Statutes.
Florida residents must obtain a license within 30 days as required by Section 322.031, Florida Statutes.

entries.title: Index (RS04)
entries.summary: Alphabetical index of all topics covered in the Driver License Operations Manual, providing quick reference to find information about licenses, permits, exams, fees, requirements, and procedures.

keyFacts.claim: The Driver License Operations Manual contains comprehensive information organized alphabetically from A to Z covering all driver license topics.
The manual includes sections on CDL medical certificates, commercial driver licenses, and commercial learner's permits.
Information is available on exams, endorsements, fees, fraud prevention, and hardship hearings.
The manual covers REAL ID requirements, restrictions, sanctions, and vision testing procedures.
Special topics include veterans designations, voluntary contributions, and requirements for persons exempt from obtaining a Florida license.

entries.title: Policy Notice Index (RS05)
entries.summary: Comprehensive index of all driver license policy notices and bulletins organized alphabetically by subject, including dates and reference numbers for topics like acceptable documents, address requirements, CDL procedures, fees, and emergency orders.

keyFacts.claim: The Policy Notice Index contains bulletins on acceptable document requirements including updates for photocopies verified through SAVE and requirements for different immigration categories.
Address change requirements have been updated multiple times, including changes from 10 days to 30 days for reporting address and name changes effective July 1, 2016.
Commercial Driver License procedures are extensively documented including Entry Level Driver Training requirements, medical certification, and hazardous materials endorsements.
Emergency orders have been issued for various natural disasters including hurricanes, tropical storms, and wildfires, providing relief from normal licensing requirements.
Financial responsibility requirements and clearance procedures are detailed in multiple bulletins covering SR22, FR44 certificates, and various sanction types.
